title: opt: quant kernels INT8/FP8 smoothquant + dequant-fusion-path + KVCache/batching improvements
author: Ethan Brooks
release_notes: Performance: faster int8/fp8 inference by enabling fused dequant paths and smoothquant-aware kernels; KV cache and continuous batching improvements reduce latency p50 and improve throughput; no API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers running quantized models (INT8/FP8 with SmoothQuant) reported suboptimal throughput and increased memory pressure when the runtime fell back to a generic dequant->matmul path. This PR introduces a fused dequant+matmul kernel for the common SmoothQuant path and a small scheduling change to bias short-tail requests to the fused path. Additionally, we align KV cache dtype handling to avoid unnecessary casts/copies when mixing INT8/FP8 model shards and improve continuous batching heuristics to maintain tight latency SLOs under mixed-size workloads.

Summary of changes: commits: - Implement fused dequant+GEMM kernel (quant_fusion.cc/h) with runtime kernel selector for INT8 and FP8 variants. - Add SmoothQuant scale-aware kernel routine and micro-optimizations for per-column scaling. - Introduce a new KernelHint enum and update kernel selector to prefer fused paths when sequence_length <= 256 and kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.6. - KVCache: change internal storage layout to store compacted int8/uint8 blobs and a separate scale metadata blob to avoid per-token conversions; add zero-copy views for decoder reuse. - Continuous batching: improve batch assembler to prioritize homogeneous dtype batches, and add a fast-path for fused kernels to bypass generic dispatcher. - Tests and benchmarks: unit tests for kernel correctness across INT8/FP8/smoothquant ranges, microbench harness updates, and end-to-end perf bench scripts.

Files changed (high level): runtime/kernels/quant_fusion.cc, runtime/kernels/quant_fusion.h, runtime/kernels/smoothquant_impl.cc, runtime/scheduler/kernel_selector.cc, runtime/kvcache/compact_storage.cc, runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cc, tests/quant/benchmarks/bench_quant_fusion.py, tests/quant/unit/test_smoothquant.py, docs/perf/quant_kernels.md, small API additions in runtime/common/types.h. (See full diff for small impl changes; PR keeps diffs focused and does not change public API).

Benchmarks and results: Microbench on rtx-a100-80gb and internal perf lab (Llama-2-70B-int8/FP8 replicas) with 512-token prompt distribution: - INT8 fused path: throughput +28% vs previous int8 fallback path, p50 latency -15%, p95 latency -8%. - FP8 fused path: throughput +18%, p50 latency -12%. - Memory: peak GPU memory reduced ~22% for inference with KV cache enabled due to compacted storage and delayed materialization. - Mixed-batch continuous batching: ~1.12x end-to-end throughput improvement under realistic mix (interactive + long-generation).

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for numerical parity (relative error thresholds) and integration tests that exercise KVCache zero-copy reuse across repeated calls. CI observed an intermittent lint failure on first run (clang-format mismatch) which was fixed in a follow-up commit. All CI checks passed on final CI run: build, unit tests, perf-smoke, sanity. The bench harness includes optional microbenchmark CI that is gated and not run on every PR.

Review conversation (high level): - Maya: requested numeric stability proofs for the fused FP8 path and a fallback safety check; author added a fast-path gate and additional unit tests covering denorms and edge scales. - Ravi: asked for KVCache compatibility notes for Dedicated/Private deployments and suggested storage migration strategy; author added migration helper and backwards-compat read shim for one release. - Olivia: flagged potential scheduler regressions under extreme mixed traffic; we added an opt-in config flag (runtime.scheduler.enable_fused_pref) and an experiment profile to A/B test rollout. Comments were resolved and approvals given.

Compatibility and rollout: This is backwards-compatible at the API level. There is a small on-disk layout change for KVCache compact storage; runtime will perform a lazy migration on first load and log a WARN. A feature-gated rollout was used in canary for one week with warmup, then globally enabled.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration/perf bench updated - [x] Docs updated (docs/perf/quant_kernels.md) - [x] Feature flag for scheduler change - [x] Migration shim for old KVCache layout

Related work / references: Linear ENG-4821 (quant kernel roadmap), ENG-4850 (kvcache storage compaction), previous PRs: pr-142837, pr-227890 which laid groundwork for kernel selection and batching.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to smoothquant edge cases (checked in tests) and verify no accuracy regressions on your model suites. If you have dedicated infra, try the canary profile before enabling globally.
